page: OVHcloud c3-16 is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz with an x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is supported by a 200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is provisioned with a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing placing in the top 25 percent at 3078.28. Text processing via Geekbench and text generation for small 135M language models also demonstrate strong performance. Multi-core CPU execution, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range. The dedicated core allocation ensures stable execution without resource contention, though the lack of hyperthreading limits parallel thread density.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3-16 offers dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources and fast NVMe storage at a competitive entry point for dedicated hardware, avoiding the overhead of shared-core models. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance suitable for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. Recommended workloads include web serving, software compilation, text processing, and small-scale database operations.
